desc: Read N, M, S, T and build adjacency lists.
Design a state representation with O(M) states.
Analyze the worst-case complexity of the proposed BFS.
Research the known optimal solution for this problem.
Verify correctness on the provided sample inputs and edge cases by running the current BFS code mentally.
Actually execute the current BFS code on the three sample inputs to confirm outputs: Sample 1 should output 3, Sample 2 should output -1, Sample 3 should output 4.
If any sample fails, debug and fix the BFS implementation.
If all samples pass, run a stress test on a worst-case star graph (N=2e5, M=2e5-1) with S=center, T=leaf to measure time/memory and determine if the solution is efficient enough.
If the BFS is too slow on worst-case inputs, redesign the algorithm to run in O(N+M) or O((N+M) log N) time (e.g., using the line graph or an auxiliary graph with O(N+M) vertices).
